notes: 139 displays and trophies in 1.0 (7 wig heads, 21 showcases, 95 trophies, 7 wall mounts, 3 display stands, 6 mannequins). Source: enshrouded.tools item pages, read from the game files (build 25988036); every recipe is likely-1.0 (datamined, not checked in game). `region` is the first region where you could make it: the latest region its recipe tree reaches (raw resources where first found, crafters where rescued, every station on the way). `comfort` is the comfort it gives (type and value), `resist` any resistance it adds, and `unlock` the site's text for what unlocks the recipe. Sizes in blocks aren't published anywhere: `size` (blocks, h and w) is on the ones measured in game. Items that stand for planner library types in base-objects.json get these details merged in by make_craft_js.py.

Ancient S.P.D.R. Construct Eye.note: Ancient S.P.D.R. Construct Eye is an Epic boss trophy material dropped by the Ancient S.P.D.R. Construct. The Hunter uses it for all four of that boss's trophies: the plain Ancient S.P.D.R. Construct Trophy and the bronze, iron and gold versions.

Wood Logs.note: Wood Logs come from chopping down trees, with bigger trees giving more, and from breaking wooden objects. Twigs and Resin drop with them. Their 166 uses include stations such as the Forge, Loom, Kitchen, Seedbed and Table Saw, crude and carved wooden furniture, doors, fences and palisades, weapon racks and wall mounts, and weapons like the Club, Spiked Club and Wooden Shield.

Cyclops Head.note: Cyclops Head goes into all four Cyclops trophies made by the Hunter: the plain Cyclops Trophy and the Bronze, Iron and Gold Cyclops Trophy versions. The head is Epic, with a stack size of 50.

Direwolf Head.note: Direwolf Head is an Epic trophy material dropped by the Direwolf boss. The Hunter turns it into the Direwolf Trophy or its bronze, iron and gold versions.

Fell Crimson Critter Queen Head.note: Fell Crimson Critter Queen Head is an Epic trophy material that only the Fell Crimson Critter Queen boss drops. It is used for the Fell Crimson Critter Queen Trophy and its bronze, iron and gold variants at the Hunter.

Fell Critter Queen Head.note: Fell Critter Queen I Head is an Epic trophy material dropped by the Fell Critter Queen I and Fell Critter Queen II bosses. The Hunter makes four trophies from it, the plain one plus bronze, iron and gold versions.

Fell Cyclops Head.note: Fell Cyclops Head drops from the Fell Cyclops in the Albaneve Summits. The Hunter uses it for the four Fell Cyclops trophies, the base Fell Cyclops Trophy and its Bronze, Iron and Gold versions.

Fell Dragon Youngling Head.note: Fell Dragon Youngling Head is taken from Fell Dragon Younglings in the Albaneve Summits. It is Epic, stacks to 50, and has four uses, all at the Hunter: the Fell Dragon Youngling trophy in plain, Bronze, Iron and Gold form.

Fell Monstrosity Head.note: Fell Monstrosity Head comes from Fell Monstrosities, which first appear in the Nomad Highlands Shroud. All four Fell Monstrosity trophies at the Hunter call for it, from the plain Fell Monstrosity Trophy through Bronze and Iron to Gold.

Fell Sicklescythe Head.note: Fell Sicklescythe Head drops from Fell Sicklescythes in the Kindlewastes Shroud. The Hunter turns it into the Fell Sicklescythe Trophy or one of its Bronze, Iron and Gold versions.

Fell Striker Head.note: Fell Striker Head drops from the Fell Striker boss. It is an Epic trophy material, and the Hunter uses it for the Fell Striker Trophy in plain, bronze, iron and gold forms.

Fell Thunderbrute Head.note: Fell Thunderbrute Head is dropped by Fell Thunderbrutes, which first show up in the Springlands Shroud. It goes into the four Fell Thunderbrute trophies made by the Hunter, up to the Gold Fell Thunderbrute Trophy.

Fell Wispwyvern Head.note: Fell Wispwyvern Head drops from the Fell Wispwyvern in the Revelwood. Its only uses are the Hunter's four Fell Wispwyvern trophies, from the base Fell Wispwyvern Trophy to the Gold one.

Hollow Cyclops Head.note: Hollow Titan Head goes into the four Hollow Cyclops trophies at the Hunter, from the base Hollow Cyclops Trophy to the Gold one. It is also needed for the Ectoplasm Press, which the Collector builds.

Hollow Titan Head.note: Hollow Titan Head is an Epic crafting material that stacks to 50.

Hollow Wispwyvern Head.note: Hollow Wispwyvern Head is an Epic trophy material from the Hollow Wispwyvern boss. The Hunter makes the Hollow Wispwyvern Trophy from it, along with bronze, iron and gold versions.

Hydrak'Dal Head.note: The Hydrak'Dal in the Veilwater Basin drops this head. Its four uses are the Hydrak'Dal Trophy at the Hunter and that trophy's Bronze, Iron and Gold versions.

Scavenger Matron Helmet.note: Scavenger Gorger Matron Helmet goes into the Hunter's four Scavenger Gorger Matron trophies, the plain Scavenger Matron Trophy and its Bronze, Iron and Gold versions. It is Epic and stacks to 50.

Scavenger Tyrant Head.note: Scavenger Tyrant Head drops from the Scavenger Tyrant boss. It is an Epic trophy material for the Scavenger Tyrant Trophy and its bronze, iron and gold versions at the Hunter.

Vorgoth's Eye.note: Vorgoth's Eye is an Epic trophy material dropped by Vorgoth, used by the Hunter for the Vorgoth's Eye Trophy and its bronze, iron and gold versions.

Vukah Brawler Head.note: Vukah Brawler Head drops from Vukah Brawlers, which appear from the Springlands onward. Besides the four Vukah Brawler trophies at the Hunter, from the plain Vukah Brawler Trophy to Gold, it is needed for the Vukah Shrine and the Scavenger Gong.

Bones.note: Bones are a common drop from wildlife and Hollow across Embervale, and bone piles, including those in and around the Hollow Halls, can be mined for more. They feed 46 recipes, among them the Flute at the Bard, Scout Pants at the Hunter, the Reaper's Wand at the Alchemist, and crypt furniture and the Bone Arrow at the Collector.

Gold Coins.note: Gold Coins are picked up in the Veilwater Basin and stack to 1,000. Many of their 17 uses are Fisher recipes: fishing rods and bait, Swimfins, and fish parts such as Fish Bones and Electric Nerve. Coffee drinks like Latte and Sweet Mokka need them too.

Torn Cloth.note: Torn Cloth comes from drops rather than crafting, and it goes into 90 recipes. These include the Bandage, the Ragged, Fur, Mage, Magician and Alchemist Apprentice armor, and the Tiny Backpack made by hand. At the Ectoplasm Press it goes into Ectoplasm, Greater Ectoplasm and Excellent Ectoplasm, and it is also used for supply sacks, war banners, showcases and stone furniture.

Metal Scraps.note: Metal Scraps are a common drop from Scavengers, and they can also be salvaged from destroyed metal objects or picked up loose in the world. They go into Nails and Metal Sheets and 112 other recipes. Those include stations such as the Forge, Kiln and Cooking Station, the Scrappy tools, the Explorer armor set, scrap pots, vats and pans, crypt torches and the Grappling Hook.

Stone.note: Stone is picked up as small stones lying on the ground all over Embervale, Shroud included. Larger stones and rock formations in the Springlands and Revelwood can be mined with a pickaxe. Its 97 uses start with the Axe, made by hand, and the Pickaxe, and run through stations such as the Forge, Kiln, Mill, Charcoal Kiln and Grinding Stones to stone furniture, coffins, statues and building blocks.

Springlands Dirt.note: Springlands Dirt is a terrain material found in the Springlands. Its 18 uses include Farm Soil at the Farmer, Workbench blocks such as the Dirt Road Block, Field Stones and Limestone Block, Springlands Rubble, Goo and White Glowing Substance at the Alchemist, the Climbing Rose and the Crucible.

Revelwood Dirt.note: Revelwood Dirt is a terrain material found in the Revelwood. The Workbench uses it for Fertile Revelwood Dirt and Revelwood Stone, the Grinding Stones for Revelwood Rubble, and it also goes into the Antique and Flint colors.

Blackmire Dirt.note: Blackmire Dirt is a terrain material that stacks to 1,000. Its one crafting use is Fertile Blackmire Dirt, made at the Workbench.

Nomad Highlands Dirt.note: Nomad Highlands Dirt is a terrain material found in the Nomad Highlands. It has five uses: Fertile Nomad Highlands Dirt and the Castle Wall Stone Block at the Workbench, Nomad Highlands Rubble at the Grinding Stones, and the Deceit and Forgotten Library colors.

Albaneve Summits Dirt.note: Albaneve Summits Dirt is the Common terrain material dug up in the Albaneve Summits, stacking to 1,000.

Veilwater Basin Dirt.note: Veilwater Basin Dirt is a terrain material found in the Veilwater Basin. It has four uses: Fertile Veilwater Basin Dirt at the Workbench, Veilwater Basin Rubble at the Grinding Stones, Wisteria at the Farmer and the Algae Seedling at the Seedbed.

Cinder's Cradle Dirt.note: Cinder's Cradle Dirt is a terrain material that stacks to 1,000. It is an ingredient of Cinder's Cradle Rubble at the Grinding Stones and of Fertile Cinder's Cradle Dirt and Fertile Altered Dirt at the Workbench.

Plant Fiber.note: Plant Fiber is gathered from bushes all over Embervale and also lies around as a loose pickup; bushes can be grown from Shrub Seedlings. Its 38 uses include the Big Straw Mat and Marksman Hood at the Hunter, the Wooden Bed and Ornate Wooden Bed at the Carpenter, Goat Food, the Cat Pillow and Sword Garden Gnome at the Farmer, and the Explosive Barrel.

Revelwood Stone.note: Revelwood Stone is a terrain material that stacks to 1,000, with 1,867 placed in the world. It goes into nine recipes, including the Kiln, the Cooking Station and Revelwood Rubble at the Grinding Stones.

Ammonia Gland.source: Fell Mushroom Crabs, Nomad Highlands Shroud and Kindlewastes Shroud

Fur Patch.note: Fur Patch is a common drop from small wildlife such as rats and bats, found all over Embervale.
